title: `os meta resync` reports a nonzero skip count with no explanation — the outcome every pre-#8692 install now sees permanently
body:
Split out of #9130, which covered the **docblock** half (delivered by PR #9183). This is the **runtime-output** half, promoted after a triage reconciliation on that card — see [the reconciliation comment](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9130#issuecomment-5310276209) for why it was initially deferred and why that deferral was withdrawn.

## The gap

After #8692's forward-only ruling (PR #9129), `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` stamps `managed_by: 'platform'` on new rows, and pre-existing `'admin'`-stamped rows are deliberately **never** migrated — a stored `'admin'` cannot be told apart from a genuine Setup takeover, so restamping could silently overwrite real admin edits.

The consequence is correct and permanent: on **every install created before that ruling**, `os meta resync` reports something like `resynced 0 / skipped 8`, forever, by design.

What an operator sees is a command that appears to do nothing, with no indication that this is the intended outcome rather than a failure. The docblock (PR #9183) now explains it — but that is documentation someone has to go looking for, and the reason they would go looking is that the output already confused them.

## Why this is not the deferrable kind of polish

The usual startup-scope test — "has anyone asked for it?" — is the wrong instrument here. This is not a feature request with speculative demand; it is a **guaranteed** recurring confusion with a known population (every pre-ruling install) and a known trigger (running a documented command). The pull is structural rather than reported.

Contrast the genuinely deferrable case, #9022: surfacing `attestedAt` / `attestedBy` in `os doctor`. Those fields have no reader and no forced encounter — nobody hits them unless they go looking. Here the operator is handed the confusing output whether or not they were curious.

## Suggested shape

One line alongside the skip summary when `skipped > 0`, naming the provenance value responsible and that it is intentional — enough that the reader stops wondering whether the command failed. Something in the shape of:

> `resynced 0 / skipped 8` — 8 row(s) are `admin`-owned and are left alone by design (see `--help`).

⛔ Deliberately **not** specifying the wording, the exact trigger condition, or whether it belongs on every run vs only when `skipped > 0` and `resynced == 0` — those are the implementing PR's call, and the surrounding output conventions in `packages/cli/src/commands/meta/resync.ts` should decide them rather than this card.

⚠️ Read the vocabulary on current `origin/main` before writing the string: `'user'` is the **legacy** spelling, normalized to `'admin'` by `normalizeManagedByVocab` (`sys-permission-set.object.ts`), so a message naming only one of them may be wrong for stored legacy rows. PR #9183's docblock handles this distinction — match it rather than inventing a second phrasing.

## Reference

- `packages/cli/src/commands/meta/resync.ts` — the skip summary
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` — the seeder docblock carrying the #8692 reasoning, and the neutral-framing log message the docblock now matches
- #9130 / PR #9183 (the docblock half) · #8692 / PR #9129 (the forward-only ruling that makes this permanent) · #9022 (the contrasting, genuinely deferred case)
